hero.title: Notes from wherever our church has traveled
hero.description: Mission trips, sabbaticals, and the occasional congregational detour this is where we keep the stories that didn't fit in a sermon. Scroll for the trip log, or jump to what's coming up next.

items.label: Packing Philosophy
items.value: One bag each, always. No exceptions.

items.label: Who Travels
items.value: Staff, elders, and volunteer teams from the congregation

items.label: Souvenir Of Choice
items.value: A local hymn book or prayer written by hand

travelKinds.heading: Four kinds of trip, four different reasons

items.title: Mission Trips
items.desc: A week or two, usually with a team from Harbor Light, building something, teaching something, or simply being present somewhere that needed us.

items.title: Staff Retreats
items.desc: Every few years the elders send our pastoral staff away for a season to rest, read, and remember why this church started doing this work in the first place.

items.title: Congregational Trips
items.desc: Half pilgrimage, half fellowship. We try to see one thing that matters to history and one thing that matters to nobody but our own church family.

items.title: Day Pilgrimages
items.desc: A drive to an old monastery, a border town, a place with one good story — gone before dinner, changed a little by evening.

trips.heading: A few places our church keeps coming back to, in memory if not in person

items.title: The year our church built a well
items.body: We sent a team for two weeks to help finish a well that had stalled for lack of funds. The project stretched on for the better part of a year, and the congregation learned more about patience from its pace than from any single sermon. There's still a photo of that first working pump on the fellowship hall wall.

items.title: Four weeks of almost nothing
items.body: Our pastoral team's first real sabbatical away together. No sermons to write, no meetings to run. Mostly walking, old prayer books, and time with people who'd been praying in that same small chapel for fifty years. They came home slower, and the congregation noticed it in the best way for months afterward.

items.title: A pilgrimage closer to home
items.body: You don't always need a passport to be changed. The rock-hewn churches here are just a four-hour drive from our own front door, and it took one of our youth group members asking why we'd never gone for the church to finally make the trip. We went the next month, candles and all.

items.title: A team, a school, a language nobody spoke
items.body: Ten days building bunk beds for a children's home with six volunteers from our congregation who'd never left Ethiopia before. Watching them fall in love with a place that shares almost nothing with home was, quietly, one of our favorite trips to send a team on.

items.q: Do you take members of the congregation on these trips?
items.a: Yes, most of them. Mission trips especially are almost always a team — we'll post an open call here and in the bulletin a few months ahead of each one.

items.q: How does the church decide where to go for a mission trip?
items.a: Usually a relationship comes first — a partner church, a missionary we already support, a need someone brought to us directly. We try not to go somewhere just because it sounded meaningful on paper.

items.q: Can I request prayer for my own upcoming trip?
items.a: Please do. Send it through the contact page or mention it Wednesday night — travel prayers are some of our favorites to pray, oddly specific as they usually are.

items.q: Does the church ever travel just for rest, with no ministry attached?
items.a: We try to, though we're not always good at it. Staff retreats are meant to be exactly that, and we're learning — slowly — to let a trip be only for rest without turning it into a project.

quote.text: Every trip our church has taken has taught us the same lesson from a different angle: God was already there before we arrived, and He'll stay long after we've gone home.
quote.attribution: Debre Selam Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus Church
